findings.summary: Scope 11 admits code compiled 'earlier for the same source, compile-time values and settings' without asking for the same specialisation (integer class, pointer alignment)
findings.detail: Point 11 (the rule page, 'Scope'; the same text in docs/SEMANTICS.md, 'Launches', and in the docstring of Rules.Compiler.Faithful) lets the code a launch runs have been compiled 'earlier for the same source, compile-time values and settings', and names as compile-time values the tl.constexpr arguments and an integer 1 or None passed to a parameter without annotation. The specialisation of the runtime arguments is in neither list: an integer argument that is a multiple of 16 is marked divisible by 16 for the compiler (SEMANTICS.md, 'Scalar arguments': 'which is true of it'), and point 6 counts each pointer's 16-byte alignment in a specialisation too. Read literally, point 11 then admits a JIT launch of add_kernel with n_elements = 98433 that runs the code compiled at an earlier launch with n_elements = 98432 (same source, same constexpr BLOCK_SIZE = 1024, n not 1, same settings), and point 6's own evidence (evidence/compiled-launch K2: n = 1001 on code compiled for n = 1024 wrote three elements past n) shows that code compiled for another specialisation need not behave as the model. vec_add_f32's Inst.ok and Pre cover every n < 2^31 and every 4-byte-aligned base, so a process that calls add on a multiple of 16 and then on another size relies on Triton's caches keying the specialisation apart, which the library does not state (SEMANTICS.md, 'Compile-time values Triton keys apart', speaks of compile-time values only). What would resolve it: point 11 and its copies also ask that reused code was compiled for the same specialisation of the runtime arguments (each argument's dtype, each integer's class, each pointer's 16-byte alignment), as point 6 does for a CompiledKernel; or the library states, with its evidence, that the JIT's in-process and on-disk keys hold the specialisation. The script's own launches (98432 and 2^12 to 2^27, all multiples of 16) stay in one class. Non-blocking: I judge the kernel as if the library were right.
findings.evidence: docs/rules/compiler-faithful.md, Scope 6 and 11; docs/SEMANTICS.md, Scalar arguments and Compile-time values Triton keys apart; docs/exclusions.md, the row on code taken from Triton's caches (for other compile-time values that share the launch's key)

(5) Module-level names: the launch reads only triton and tl (lines 23-24, kernel lines, mapped); host lines 86-87 bind x and y, but the kernel assigns its own x and y at lines 50-51 before its only read at line 52, and the host lines bind nothing else the launch reads.
